**Finding submitted: IP — missing (critical).**

**What I checked.** I read the whole agreement (all five sections) and ran targeted searches for ownership, title, intellectual property, assignment, licence and data language. Responsive locations:

- §§1.1–1.3, 1.6 (p0005–p0007): HDI designs, develops, hosts and bears all costs of the bespoke Deerskin Site — no ownership stated.
- §2.1 (p0016): the Company supplies all Content — no reservation of rights.
- §5.2 (p0032): editorial/artistic control and approval rights only — control, not ownership.
- §5.3 (p0033): title language limited to physical Deerskin Products.
- §6.1 (p0038–p0039): narrow, non-exclusive Marks licence to HDI with an express "no other licences" carve-out — this benefits us, so not flagged.
- §8.1/8.2 (p0048, p0053): Content, user information and data protected only as Confidential Information — confidentiality is not ownership.
- §10.2 (p0062) rules out co-ownership of the *relationship*, not of IP.

**Why missing rather than deviation.** There is no assignment, no licence back, and no Customer Data ownership sentence anywhere; HDI as developer and host would retain rights in the site it builds and de facto control of our customer/transaction data. That fails every fallback element as well as the preferred position, so the rule's expected clause simply does not exist.

**The change.** One new Section 5.5 inserted after p0035 (inside "Site; Site Management"), carrying all eight preferred elements in four sentences: Company ownership of the Site/Content/deliverables and work product, HDI's assignment, HDI's retention of pre-existing IP, a perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free licence to embedded HDI IP, Company retention of all user, customer and transaction data, and no joint ownership. The comment offers the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense) if HDI insists on keeping title to its platform. Redline validated `ok:true` with the minimality gate clear; no neighbouring text was rewritten.
